content.text: { "protocol": "dcp/1.0", "kind": "contribution", "exchange": "02997a55-947e-4f99-b094-757b16511029", "intent": "answer", "replyTargets": [], "composition": [ { "id": "new:b1", "kind": "paragraph", "markup": "Your impression captures something important: Ludovico offered Leonardo opportunities that went well beyond painting. But entering the court was probably a gradual process, rather than a single, securely documented appointment.", "ranges": [], "textStyle": null, "margins": null }, { "id": "new:b2", "kind": "heading", "markup": "How Leonardo entered the court", "ranges": [ { "id": "new:s1", "type": "mutable/entity-reference", "from": "4", "to": "12", "ref": "new:e1", "attributes": [] } ], "level": 2, "textStyle": null, "margins": null }, { "id": "new:b3", "kind": "paragraph", "markup": "Leonardo moved from Florence to Milan around 1482. Ludovico Sforza was then becoming the effective ruler of the duchy, although he did not formally become duke until 1494. A famous surviving draft letter, usually dated about 1482, shows Leonardo pitching himself chiefly as a military engineer: portable bridges, siege equipment, artillery and defensive works dominate it. Painting appears only near the end, alongside sculpture and a proposed equestrian monument.", "ranges": [], "textStyle": null, "margins": null }, { "id": "new:b4", "kind": "paragraph", "markup": "The letter is evidence of an approach, not proof of an immediate appointment: we do not know whether that particular draft was delivered. Later accounts also connect Leonardo’s arrival with his skill as a musician and a remarkable lyre, but those details are less secure. What is clear is that he gradually established himself within the Sforza court as a versatile artist, designer and engineer.", "ranges": [], "textStyle": null, "margins": null }, { "id": "new:b5", "kind": "heading", "markup": "Major projects during the first Milanese period", "ranges": [], "level": 2, "textStyle": null, "margins": null }, { "id": "new:b6", "kind": "list", "style": "bullet", "items": [ [ { "id": "new:b7", "kind": "paragraph", "markup": "The equestrian monument to Francesco Sforza. Ludovico wanted a colossal bronze memorial to his father, Francesco Sforza. Leonardo spent years studying horses and casting methods, and displayed a full-scale clay model in 1493. The bronze statue was never cast; metal intended for it was diverted to military needs.", "ranges": [], "textStyle": null, "margins": null } ], [ { "id": "new:b8", "kind": "paragraph", "markup": "The Last Supper, about 1495–1498. Executed for the refectory of Santa Maria delle Grazie, the painting formed part of Ludovico’s patronage of a religious complex intended as a dynastic burial place. Leonardo’s experimental technique on a dry wall allowed painstaking revision, but contributed to its early deterioration.", "ranges": [], "textStyle": null, "margins": null } ], [ { "id": "new:b9", "kind": "paragraph", "markup": "Court spectacles and decoration. Leonardo designed theatrical machinery, costumes and elaborate entertainments that advertised the court’s magnificence. He also worked on the Sala delle Asse in the Sforza Castle in 1498, transforming the room with an illusionistic canopy of interlaced trees.", "ranges": [], "textStyle": null, "margins": null } ], [ { "id": "new:b10", "kind": "paragraph", "markup": "Engineering and technical studies. His work included surveys and designs concerning waterways, hydraulic machinery, fortifications and military technology. Here it is important to distinguish proposals and notebook investigations from completed works: not every ingenious drawing became a project built for Ludovico.", "ranges": [], "textStyle": null, "margins": null } ], [ { "id": "new:b11", "kind": "paragraph", "markup": "Other major painting in Milan. Leonardo began The Virgin of the Rocks following a 1483 commission from the Confraternity of the Immaculate Conception. It belongs to this period, but was not a commission from Ludovico—a useful reminder that working in Milan and working directly for the court were not identical.", "ranges": [], "textStyle": null, "margins": null } ] ], "configuration": null }, { "id": "new:b12", "kind": "paragraph", "markup": "Leonardo’s first Milanese period ended in 1499, when French forces overthrew Ludovico’s regime. The relationship’s distinctive feature was its breadth: Leonardo could offer his patron military utility, technical ingenuity, spectacular entertainment and lasting artistic prestige.", "ranges": [], "textStyle": null, "margins": null } ], "anchors": [ { "id": "new:r1", "source": "src:pK_8IQrC4kpOY6am07f6EA:b2", "revision": "217f7614-5613-4584-8176-3c49a99fed23", "selector": { "exact": "Ludovico
